checkpoints.description: [1/4] Pre-register ADR-021 and add failing tests for radial rays at the acoustic horizon

impact_assessment.why: The horizon metric is established, but its causal structure has not been checked: radial rays should change direction at r_H and peel away with the surface gravity rate. This tests the analogue horizon beyond the metric components.
impact_assessment.benefits: A positive causal-structure result: the horizon is a separatrix, the peeling rate equals c^2/r_H, and the ray times match the analytic solution.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 30, no existing claim changes; dependency: numpy only; concurrency: none; state: one result file; numerical: the ray speed vanishes at r_H, so the integration must stop before r_H
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use the valid Q=0.05, h=0.1 regime; derive the analytic ray time; compare RK4 to it; test the sign of the speed on both sides and the peeling rate

checkpoints.description: [3/4] Radial rays: outgoing speed signs -0.110/+0.090 across r_H; ray times match analytic to 2e-6; peeling rate 12.209936 equals surface gravity; claim 30 PROVEN

impact_assessment.why: The horizon is established analytically and by rays. A numerical wave-scattering test checks that a right-moving packet is blocked at the horizon in the valid long-wavelength regime.
impact_assessment.benefits: A direct numerical demonstration of horizon blocking, with a uniform-flow control that transmits; it complements the metric and ray results.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 31, no existing claim changes; dependency: numpy only; concurrency: none; state: one result file; numerical: the prescribed 1D flow is kinematic and not a consistent shallow-water equilibrium
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use Riemann invariants with upwind advection and a sponge; test a uniform-flow control; pre-register transmitted fraction <1e-3 at the horizon and >0.2 in the control; state the kinematic limitation

[1/4] Pre-register ADR-023 and add failing tests for the hydrated-electron cavity scale

impact_assessment.why: Water's dielectric constant and surface tension are two of its distinctive properties. A screened hydrogen state gives a 41.5 Å, 2.2 meV atom; the balance of electron quantum pressure and surface tension gives a 2.86 Å cavity and 0.93 eV, close to the hydrated electron scale. This is a scale test, not a derivation of the 1.7 eV absorption.
impact_assessment.benefits: A positive water-property link to a real quantum particle, with explicit model limits.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 32, no existing claim changes; dependency: numpy only; concurrency: none; state: one result file; data: the 1.7 eV hydrated-electron absorption is a literature value, so the comparison is a scale test
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use water at 20 C; derive the cavity minimum analytically; compare the screened hydrogen, capillary cavity and infinite-well scales; state that the 0.93 eV result is a factor 1.8 below the observed 1.7 eV

checkpoints.description: [3/4] Hydrated electron: screened hydrogen a*=41.5 A, E=-2.2 meV; capillary cavity R=2.858 A, E=0.933 eV vs observed 1.7 eV (factor 1.8); claim 32 NUMERIC (cavity scale match)

[1/4] Pre-register ADR-024 and add failing tests for the finite spherical well; predict no 1p at R=2.858 A/Born, maximum Born-depth s->p gap 0.615 eV, and required depth 3.715 eV at R=3.181 A

impact_assessment.why: Claim 32 gives the hydrated-electron cavity scale but not the 1.7 eV absorption. The minimal closure is a finite spherical well with the Born solvation depth; it either supports a 1p state near 1.7 eV or falsifies the bound-bound interpretation.
impact_assessment.benefits: A decisive test of the simplest cavity model, a quantitative required-depth target for the next polaron/band-offset model, and a clean negative result rather than a tuned fit.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 33, no existing claim changes; dependency: math and numpy only; concurrency: none; state: one result file; model: minimal finite well with no polaron correction; data: the 1.7 eV absorption is a literature anchor
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pre-register the exact predictions, use an analytic threshold check (kappa=pi for 1p), scan the depth and radius, report the maximum Born-depth gap and the minimum required depth, and state the model limits explicitly

[1/4] Pre-register ADR-025 and add failing tests for the finite-well bound-free absorption; predict a Born-depth continuum peak at 1.025 eV (sum rule 0.992) and an extra depth of 1.198 eV for a 1.7 eV peak

impact_assessment.why: Claim 33 rules out the bound-bound 1s->1p interpretation. The observed hydrated-electron band is broad, so the remaining natural channel is bound-free 1s->p absorption. The same finite well makes a parameter-free prediction for the continuum peak, which can be tested against the 1.7 eV anchor.
impact_assessment.benefits: A validated continuum calculation (TRK sum rule) and a quantitative extra-depth target; it tests whether the 1.7 eV feature can be a bound-free transition without inventing a bound 1p state.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 34, no existing claim changes; dependency: numpy only; concurrency: none; state: one result file; model: same finite well, no new potential; numerical: the dipole integral needs a converged grid and sum-rule check; data: the 1.7 eV absorption is a literature anchor
impact_assessment.mitigation: Work in atomic units, validate the continuum normalization with the TRK sum rule (~1), converge the peak against grid size and tail, pre-register the Born-depth peak and the extra-depth inversion, and state that the extra depth is a target rather than a derived correction
